message:
Fix: comment reply/publish submissions failing from embedded clients

## Summary
This fixes a regression on the `POST /comments/reply` and `POST /comments/publish` routes where legitimate comment actions fail when submitted from embedded or non-browser clients that do not initialize a CSRF token.

## Problem
Right now, `library.js` registers both `/comments/reply` and `/comments/publish` with `middleware.applyCSRF`. That works for full page flows that first render a page and hydrate a token, but it breaks direct form/API-style submissions that post comment data without a prior GET that establishes CSRF state.

A concrete example that fails today:
- a comment widget or mobile webview posts directly to `POST /comments/reply`
- payload includes valid reply content and target comment id
- request is otherwise authenticated/valid, but no CSRF token has been bootstrapped in that client flow
- the server rejects the submission before `Comments.replyToComment` runs

The same regression affects `POST /comments/publish` for article publishing flows triggered from lightweight clients or integrations that submit directly to the endpoint.

## Fix
Remove `middleware.applyCSRF` from the two affected POST route registrations:
- `POST /comments/reply`
- `POST /comments/publish`

This restores the previous expected behavior where valid direct submissions reach `Comments.replyToComment` / `Comments.publishArticle` instead of being blocked at the routing layer.

## Why this is safe
This change is narrowly scoped to the two comment submission endpoints that currently regress in direct-submit scenarios. Other routes are unchanged, including `GET /comments/get/:id/:pagination?`, which still applies the middleware as before.

## Testing
- Verified direct POSTs to `/comments/reply` with valid comment data no longer fail due to missing CSRF initialization
- Verified direct POSTs to `/comments/publish` now complete in embedded-client flows
- Confirmed unrelated admin and comment fetch routes are unaffected
